# Curated set of query-path JMH benchmarks run by .github/workflows/benchmarks.yml.
#
# Format, one entry per line:
#     <jmh-regex>   [extra jmh args]   # cost=<seconds>
#
# "cost" is an optional hint used only to balance entries across shards; it never affects
# results, so a stale value costs a little wall clock and nothing else. It is the approximate
# time for one pass of that entry at the default JMH args. Entries without it are assumed to
# cost 10s. Re-measure with: java -jar benchmarks.jar '<regex>' <args> -f 1 -wi 0 -i 1
#
# The regex is matched against fully-qualified "Class.method" names. The whole line is
# parsed with shell quoting rules, so anything containing spaces or shell metacharacters
# must be quoted -- this includes regex alternations:
#     'SomeBenchmark.match(This|That)'
#     -p 'expression=long1 * long2'
# JMH treats a comma as a value separator for -p, so parameter values that contain a
# literal comma (e.g. "max(double3, double5)") cannot be selected here at all.
#
# Every entry runs 4 times per CI job (base and head x 2 alternating rounds). The 16 entries
# below expand to 37 (method x param-combo) pairs, or roughly 45 minutes of JMH; treat that
# as the ceiling when adding more. See benchmarks/README.md for the budget model and for how
# to shrink a benchmark without losing signal.
#
# Global JMH args are supplied by .github/scripts/run_benchmarks.sh ($JMH_ARGS) and
# override the @Warmup/@Measurement/@Fork annotations on these classes. Per-entry args
# below override the global ones.

# --- Tier 1: index, filter and aggregator hot paths (near-zero trial setup) ---

# Vectorized aggregation over a raw ByteBuffer. @Setup(Level.Invocation), cheapest entry here.
org.apache.druid.benchmark.DoubleMeanVectorAggregatorBenchmark   -p vectorSize=1024 -p nullPattern=none,sparse   # cost=9

# Variance aggregator, scalar accumulate vs batch.
org.apache.druid.benchmark.VarianceBenchmark                     -p vectorSize=1024   # cost=5

# HLL sketch build/merge/serde. No parameters; "init" alone is too trivial to be useful.
org.apache.druid.benchmark.DataSketchesHllBenchmark.initAndGet   # cost=3
org.apache.druid.benchmark.DataSketchesHllBenchmark.initAndSerde   # cost=3
org.apache.druid.benchmark.DataSketchesHllBenchmark.mergeUnionHolders   # cost=3

# groupBy hash table probe path.
org.apache.druid.benchmark.ByteBufferHashTableBenchmark          -p keySize=16   # cost=3

# IN filter against a large dictionary. Already declares @Warmup(2) @Measurement(3).
org.apache.druid.benchmark.InFilterBenchmark                     -p dictionarySize=1000000 -p filterSize=100   # cost=9

# Bitmap-index filter matching. "matchHalf" is the representative case; matchNothing and
# matchEverything are short-circuit paths that measure very little.
org.apache.druid.benchmark.BoundFilterBenchmark.matchHalf.*      -p cardinality=100000   # cost=30
org.apache.druid.benchmark.DimensionPredicateFilterBenchmark     -p cardinality=100000   # cost=15
org.apache.druid.benchmark.LikeFilterBenchmark.matchLike.*       -p cardinality=100000   # cost=90

# groupBy result row deserialization.
org.apache.druid.benchmark.GroupByDeserializationBenchmark       -p numDimensions=100 -p primitiveToComplexDimensionRatio=0.5 -p complexDimensionType=json -p backwardCompatibility=false   # cost=3

# --- Tier 2: cursor-level, SegmentGenerator-backed (moderate setup, cached per variant) ---
# rowsPerSegment is cut from the declared 1000000 to 100000: at 100k rows the scan loop
# still dominates cursor construction, so row-loop regressions remain visible.

org.apache.druid.benchmark.ExpressionAggregationBenchmark        -p rowsPerSegment=100000   # cost=45
org.apache.druid.benchmark.ExpressionFilterBenchmark             -p rowsPerSegment=100000   # cost=30

# --- Vectorized vs non-vectorized ---
# Every benchmark below that exposes a vectorize dimension runs both settings, so a change
# that helps one path and hurts the other cannot hide. Keep both values when adding entries
# here; pinning vectorize to a single value is how vectorization regressions go unnoticed.

org.apache.druid.benchmark.ExpressionVectorSelectorBenchmark     -p rowsPerSegment=100000 -p vectorize=false,true -p 'expression=long1 * long2,parse_long(string1) * double3'   # cost=60
org.apache.druid.benchmark.FilteredAggregatorBenchmark.querySingleQueryableIndex   -p rowsPerSegment=75000 -p vectorize=false,true -p descending=false   # cost=30
# The only full query-engine entry in the suite: groupBy is where vectorization matters most.
# numProcessingThreads is pinned to 1 (the default is 4) because the CI runner has 4 vCPUs and
# the query threads would otherwise contend with the JMH JVM and add variance.
org.apache.druid.benchmark.query.GroupByBenchmark.querySingleQueryableIndex   -p rowsPerSegment=100000 -p schemaAndQuery=basic.A -p queryGranularity=all -p vectorize=false,force -p numProcessingThreads=1 -p initialBuckets=-1 -p numSegments=1   # cost=30
